result.summary: Adds a functional test verifying that during Initial Block Download (IBD), outbound full-relay and block-relay-only peers are disconnected when their headers chain does not meet nMinimumChainWork. It also asserts that manual and inbound peers serving insufficient chain work remain connected.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's logic for disconnecting outbound peers with insufficient chain work during IBD was untested in the functional test suite, because functional tests default to minimum chain work of zero and typically connect peers manually.
evidence: Author description: 'While in IBD, outbound peers (full-relay and block-relay-only) whose headers chain has less work than `nMinimumChainWork` are disconnected. This behavior was not covered by any test, since the functional tests only connect nodes to each other via manual connections, and the default minimum chain work is zero.'
result.card: Adds a test verifying that during IBD, outbound full-relay and block-relay-only peers whose chain work is below -minimumchainwork are disconnected, while inbound and manual connections are retained. The existing codebase lacked test coverage for this eviction logic because functional tests typically use manual connections and default to zero minimum chain work. No dependencies are stated.
uncertainties: Diff was omitted from the prompt, so specific test file and implementation details cannot be verified directly.

risk.why: Only modifies or adds Python functional tests, posing no risk to release binaries or consensus.
